utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. And good morning to you, Madam Registrar, if you are not included amongst the "everybody." Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record today’s accused Pandurevic is absent. We were informed beforehand of his absence and waiver is in our hands. This will apply for today and tomorrow, if I remember well. Prosecution today is represented by Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. There's no one else I think. From amongst the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Petrusic and Mr. Haynes. And Mr. Josse. Professor, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry we had to keep you here another day. We'll soon finish with you and then you can go home to your family. Mr. Vanderpuye, good morning to you, if you could conclude your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you, good morning, Your Honours, good morning to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Dr. Bajagic. If I could have please, 65 ter 3793 in e-court. While that's loading, doctor, I had asked you a series of questions yesterday concerning a report that was written by Mr. Borovcanin dated 30th June, and I think the second one was 1 July. I want to show you this report which was written on the -- well, it's written actually on the 30th of June, and the document number or the dispatch number is 113/95. Now, you can see in this document that it reports or it was directed to the police staff in Pale, police forces staff in Vogosca and Janja special police brigade. What it reports here, if you can see that in the copy on the right, is it reports on the 29th of June, a combat group comprised of the 4th special police detachment 7th special police detachment, Kajman police detachment, Serbian MUP, along with the VRS offensive forces launched an attack in Lucevik facility, which is under the enemy's control and is of extreme importance for the control of the Trnovo-Sarajevo road. It goes on to report about combat, if you look down in the English version it's in the third paragraph, and I think it should correspond with the version in B/C/S as well, but in any event, you can see that the beginning of the paragraph you find the date 6/29, June 29th, 1995. In any event, it reports there that during combats on the 29th of June, two members of the special police detachment from the 4th and 7th and two members of the Serbian MUP were wounded. We go to the next page in the English, I think it's near the bottom of the page in the B/C/S version, you'll see that he reports, "Given the additional PJP forces, given that the additional PJP forces had been deployed in the previous days following the break-through of the VRS lines towards Trnovo, we are now trying to restore the previous status of the zone of responsibility of the police. Six PJP companies are now being engaged and three companies were holding the line 20 days ago." I asked you some questions I think -- well, yesterday for certain, regarding your assessment of whether or not Mr. Borovcanin is commanding these particular units. In light of what you have seen in this document, does that help you in any way to determine his position in respect of those units, and as concerns this report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the document carefully, as I did yesterday. Towards the bottom it says Ljubisa Borovcanin, deputy commander of the SBP. Therefore, Mr. Borovcanin sent this report to three addressees. From this it still cannot be seen whether he is commanding all of the units mentioned herein. For me, it can also mean that he is only commanding the parts of the special police brigade that were in that area rather than all of the units mentioned in their letter. Based on that, I can't see from the document that he is actually in command of all the units referred to. However, I can make a presumption, with a degree of certainty, that the police detachments mentioned that are part of the Republika Srpska special police brigade that he is in command of those. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right, Doctor. If I could have in e-court, please, 65 ter 57. All right. This is an order, if you look at the bottom it's signed by staff commander Tomislav Kovac. I think we mentioned him yesterday. It is directed to the special police brigade, staff of the Trnovo police forces command, staff of the Vogosca police forces command, et cetera. You can read it, it's on the screen. In particular, you can see from this document that in paragraph or point number 3 that Ljubomir Borovcanin and deputy commander of the special police brigade is designated as the commander of the MUP units, and in paragraph 2 you can see the MUP units under whose command he is -- whose command he is to assume. And that consists of the 2nd police detachment from Sekovici, you see that, 1st Company PJP unit of the Zvornik, and then it says mixed company of joint RSK and Serbian RS MUP forces from the -- and a company of the training camp from Jahorina. In fact, you refer to this order in your report. You agree this report puts Mr. Borovcanin in command of those units; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious from the document, from this order issued by deputy minister or staff commander of the police forces at the headquarters, it is clear from the letter that Mr. Borovcanin was to assume command over the units referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And per this order, you can see also that it directs Mr. Borovcanin as unit commander to make contact with the corps Chief of Staff General Krstic. That is the order; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says, with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as per this order, then, Mr. Borovcanin were to have followed it, he would be under the -- under the command of General Krstic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. Once in the field he was to get in touch with General Krstic, he was to report to him and as of that moment resubordination takes place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have in e-court please, 65 ter 3789. Okay. As you can see, this is a document the Prosecution has recently identified and it is dated 13 July 1995. Now, I don't think you can see it on your -- if you go down on the B/C/S version, you can see that this is a document that is type signed Ljubisa Borovcanin, it is dated the 13th of July 1995, and its number is 284/95. This particular report it is directed to the Pale police staff and the special police brigade Janja. What it does is it recounts events during the course of the day, it says that the MUP combat unit composed of the 2nd detachment, the MUP company of the Zvornik PJP and a mixed company of the Janja MUP is engaged in offensive actions from the direction of Zuti Most towards Potocari, at 5.30 we sealed off the checkpoint from Zuti Most and we then proceeded along the road towards Potocari. It's clear as per the previous order that Mr. Borovcanin is in command of these units; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to that order, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm referring to the 10 July order from Tomislav Kovac that I just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in this particular 13 July report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to interrupt my colleague, really, he is cross-examining, it's not fair maybe but I would just like to have a clear record on this. Here we have in paragraph 1 mixed company of MUP Janja which does not correspond to the previous document and also units which were mentioned in previous document in relation to MUP of Republika Srpska Krajina and Serbia are not mentioned in this one so just to have a clear record on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do apologise, Mr. President, I don't have the transcript running in front of me. I was looking at the document as I was reading it. And I can't find it right now so I'll just read it again. This document that is the 13th of July, speaks about a mixed company of the Janja MUP, that's what the translation I have says. The order from 10 July speaks about a mixed company of joint RSK Serbian and RS MUP and a company from the training camp of Jahorina. My question to the expert is, is it clear from this document that he is in command of these units, as per the previous order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, fair enough, fair enough. But it's clear now while it wasn't that clear before, Mr. Lazarevic was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate the intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you understand the question now, sir? Are you able to answer it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we understood each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you don't have -- in other words, based upon what we've just said now your answer hasn't changed any, has it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin commanded those units referred to in the order of the 10th of July, 1995. I can't place these two texts on the screen to see whether the units mentioned in one are all referred to in the other. In the first one we have the first company of the PJP and then we have Janja here. I don't think it appeared in the previous order, but if I had both documents on the screen, I'd be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can move. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to this document, that is the 13 July 1995 document, 284/95, it is directed to the Pale police staff. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see, it was sent to three addressees, Pale police staff, Vogosca police staff and the special police brigade in Janja. Three addressees. I think this is a very short information letting them know where the individual units are. It is a document sent by Mr. Borovcanin informing people that those units were there and there at that location. If there was a mixed company from Janja in the area where he was, it was only natural that he would let the special police brigade in Janja know. It is a document by way of which he is informing whether the individual units of the police are and how they fared in combat that day. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And the police staff, the Pale police staff, who is that composed of? I mean, what is it and who comprises it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to go back to the document. I can't tell you off the cuff. I don't know what the composition of the staff is. I can't memorize so many names. In any case, it is a police staff of the Ministry of the Interior. It can be nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you can see in this report, and although it's unclear to you whether or not Mr. Borovcanin command all of the units that are in it, but if he is not commanding all of the units that are in it, he is certainly reporting about units that he doesn't command. That's fair to say; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And let me ask --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not reporting but informing, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the units that he is in command of, that would be a report, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know because of the order of the 10th of July as of the moment when he was reporting to General Krstic, I think it was General Krstic, as of that moment, he was resubordinated to the unit of the RS army in whose area of responsibility he was with his unit. In that regard, he is duty-bound to submit mandatory reports to that structure rather than to the Ministry of the Interior. That is why I said that he was informing by this document, rather than reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is clear then, that he is duty-bound to report on those units that he commands as per the rules; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in the instruction on regular, urgent and statistical reporting, there are no situations foreseen that would cover resubordination. I don't remember such provisions in the instruction of the Ministry of the Interior on the regular, urgent and statistical reporting. I don't think it contains provisions which could reflect this situation. Hence, I can only speculate on his obligations and duties. Perhaps the rules were placed ad hoc, but I did not come across that while drafting my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You couldn't find a rule that obligates the commander of MUP units that are subordinated to the VRS to report on their status to the army or to the Ministry of the Interior? You couldn't find a rule?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the instruction as regards informing and reporting within the MUP. Any document that would refer to a situation like this is something I have not come across and read, unfortunately. Had I been able to, perhaps I would have been able to answer this differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you, does the concept of unity of command, does that apply to MUP combat forces?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what unity of command are you referring to. I'm not clear on the term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In which circumstances, that would be a fair question to the witness. But still he didn't understand the question, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If the witness knows, and the specific circumstances I'm talking about are combat forces, combat forces of the MUP. I think I did state that in my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's proceed. Go ahead. He needs to answer the question when I said let's proceed. Are you in a position to answer that question, Professor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If we are talking about the other parts of the units of the Ministry of the Interior which are independent in combat as part of the armed forces they must observe the instruction on all sorts of reporting. There's no doubt about that. So if we are talking about units of the Ministry of the Interior outside of this unit, they will have to abide by the instruction of the Ministry of the Interior about urgent, statistical and occasional reporting. Urgent means by dispatches, occasional reporting, statistical reporting, all sorts of reporting that have to be abided by.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir. You were asked a series of questions on your direct examination yesterday concerning the rules on internal organisation of the MUP. I wanted to put to you some questions regarding that, if I may. Under Article 51 of the rules on internal organisation of the MUP, that was 4D144. It is clear that the general obligations of members or employees of the MUP, it is that they are entrusted or obliged to carry out thoroughly, orderly and in a timely fashion, meeting high standards and responsibly, their duties and tasks in a manner that is in accordance with all legal and other regulations as well as the instructions received from the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose if you are reading, but I don't have anything in front of me in an electronic form. I can't see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you would like me to put it up, I'll put it up there for you. It's 4D144. There is no English, I'll have to have him read it into the record. I understood that my colleagues were going to provide a fully translated version of the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can survive that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the fully translated version? In any event, in the B/C/S version it's page -- I believe it's page 32 in e-court. 5705 is the ERN number so we can page forward I think three pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is 5702. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Article 51 is at the bottom of the page -- now it's in the middle of the page. If you can take a look at that and read it into the record?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. Article 51: "An employee is duty-bound to perform duties and tasks that he is entrusted with in time at a high quality level, economically, with responsibility and in keeping with the legal and other regulations as well as the instructions provided by the ministry." Yes, I am clear on this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that applies to all members of the Ministry of the Interior, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And with respect to the law on the internal organisation of the MUP, that was 4D172, Article 15 of that document provides that the protection of citizens' lives and personal safety as well as the prevention and detection of criminal offences a responsibility to be discharged by members of the MUP. And that's among other things, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I don't see the article on the screen but I agree with it. This article sums up and defines the overall function of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that article didn't change with respect to the update of the law in March 1994 or subsequently; right? I see we have it in e-court, Article 15, starts with the public security service carries out administrative, specialized and other activities, and if you continue down you can see that among those responsibilities concern -- administrative responsibilities concerns the protection of citizens' lives and personal safety and the prevention and detection of criminal offences. You see that, right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is absolutely correct, I'm very familiar with Article 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well. So you know that it didn't change in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see how this article could undergo any major changes. It has to remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Article 41 of the same law on the internal organisation of the MUP, that provides for an oath or a pledge of authorised officials of the Ministry of the Interior; right? You find that on page 6 in the English and page 6 in the B/C/S. English if you look down at the bottom of the page, you can see it begins with the sentence "The text of the formal statement reads:" It provides: "I hereby pledge to execute the duties of an authorised official in a conscientious and responsible manner, to adhere to the constitution and the law, to protect with all my strength the constitutionally established order of the republic, the rights, freedoms and security, and to carry out these and other activities and tasks of an authorised other officials even when the execution of such tasks places my life in danger."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it and I'm familiar with this text, I know of it, I know that it is part of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is required to be undertaken and discharged by authorised members of the Ministry of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also were asked some questions as concerns the constitution, and in particular you read part of Article 68 of the constitution, I think --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you know that Article 68 provides, it provides for the protection of human rights, national freedom and equality, constitutionality and legality?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That was provided for in the constitution of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also with respect to the constitution of the Republika Srpska; is that right? You have to answer on the record.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in Article 51 of that constitution, it refers to what is called the constitutional order. I refer you to that because the oath refers to the protection of the constitutional order, and Article 5 of the constitution defines the constitutional order in part that it's based on the protection of ethnic groups and other minorities. You recall that; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it's there, but I cannot remember off the cuff which article it is. It's impossible for me to bear all these extensive documents in my memory, but I know that it's part of the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me put it up on the screen so you can see it. It's 4D194. I think it might be right on page 1. Page 2 in the English, I think. If you look at Article 5, the very last point it says the protection of ethnic groups and other minorities. Article 5 reads: "Constitutional order of the republic is based on the following," and it lists a number of things. You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it and I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And let me just point out the very first item on this. What that reads is: "The constitutional order of the republic is based on," and the very first item is "the guarantee and protection of human freedom and rights with respect to international standards." You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the Geneva Conventions would be considered international standards as referred to in this document; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just refer you back to Article 4 of the law on internal organisation of the MUP. 4D172 in e-court. It's on page 6 in the B/C/S and page 6 in the English. Article 42 provides -- I wish we could blow it up a little bit. "Authorised officials must carry out activities and tasks related to the protection of the constitutional order," as I've just read it to you. "... protection of national lives, personal security, the prevention of criminal offences and capture of their perpetrators as well as activities and tasks related to maintaining law and order at all times, regardless of whether they are on duty and whether they have been explicitly assigned a particular task." You see that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And all authorised members of the MUP are obligated to comply with this rule?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no further questions for you, Doctor, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Vanderpuye. Is there redirect, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that it will be like 25 to 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning Dr. Bajagic again.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to start my re-examination with last things first, i.e., with the questions that my learned friend Mr. Vanderpuye put to you a minute ago and showed you some relevant paragraphs about the Ministry of the Interior and all these relevant paragraphs that he quoted to you represent the duties as well as the authorities of the authorised officials of the Ministry of the Interior under the law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My question about these paragraphs is as follows: When a member of the Ministry of the Interior performs his regular duties and tasks, he has all the authorities that we have just had an opportunity to look at?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to a different situation now. It is a situation in which a member of the Ministry of the Interior participates as a resubordinated member within a unit of the Ministry of the Interior, in combat, would he still have the same authorities that are prescribed by the law or not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He cannot have standard authorities if he is resubordinated and participates in combat under the command of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, while there is combat going on and while the unit of the Ministry of the Interior is participating in combat, the officials of the Ministry of the Interior do not have the same authorities as they would normally have?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First of all I object to the question. It's clearly leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The other issue is with respect to this particular -- it's unclear what particular authorities and obligations my colleague is referring to in either the question or the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you wish to comment, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think. I was speaking about authorities that police officers have in regular situation and to compare it with the situation in combat activities when resubordinating and when participating in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We leave it in your hands, Mr. Lazarevic, to expand on this to make it a little bit more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I could put one hypothetical question to the witness, I will put it and Your Honours will decide whether this question is fair. Of course my colleague are allowed to intervene if they find it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are almost inviting him to object beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are not hearing the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we haven't got translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Professor Bajagic, let's take into account the following hypothetical situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you now receiving interpretation, can you follow me?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Professor Bajagic, let's take, for example, an inspector working in crime prevention service in the security centre in Zvornik, for example. His main task would be -- what would it be, could you tell me what would be such an inspector's main task?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To detect and apprehend perpetrators of crime, of general crime, it would rather depend on the particular area he works on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in performing these tasks and duties, what would be his authorities under the law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would have all the authorities that we have already listed from the law of the interior issuing warning, issuing orders, enforcement, the use of firearms, all such authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. So these authorities are such when he is on duty and when he is off duty, wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at a situation in which the same inspector has become a member of a special police unit and/or a PJP and becomes a member of a special company of the police, and that special company participates in combat as a unit resubordinated to the army command. In such a situation, would this inspector maintain the same authorities that he had before?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it loud and clear even before this very detailed question was put to me. He would no longer have such authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For how long? For how long would he not have such authorities?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the moment he returned to his normal position and to the moment when he performs his normal tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While he participates in combat, does he have an official ID?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he cannot identify himself as a police member if he participates in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will move on to some other topics that were tackled yesterday. Yesterday on pages 56 to 62 of the transcript, my learned friend Ostojic asked you something about informing and reporting and he quoted Article 256 of your expert report. This is Exhibit 4D499, page 66 in B/C/S and pages 67 and 68 in English. And let's just clarify something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment. I need to discuss something with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before going further I was about to ask the witness to clarify his explanation. Instead of taking the example of inspector, why don't we just take the example of Mr. Borovcanin. He was a deputy commander of the special police brigade, and he was designated by Mr. Kovac to command the several MUP units as we saw earlier and he was resubordinated to Mr. Krstic. How is new role of Mr. Borovcanin different from the previous one in concrete terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is different because my previous explanation applies to Mr. Borovcanin. Mr. Borovcanin was resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska and he no longer had the same authorities and he could not act on the ground as a policeman, irrespective of his function as a member of the ministry of the interior for as long as he is resubordinated to somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he is still in command -- he is in command of those several MUP units, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not in dispute, but we are not talking about any police authorities or anything that had to do with that, that we have just spoken about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While being resubordinated to the VRS, he is also duty-bound to report to the -- his superiors in the MUP as we have seen in one of his reports or information sent to his Pale police staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see we are talking at cross purposes. When he is resubordinated to the army, Mr. Borovcanin can just be incorporated in the system of informing and reporting of the Army of Republika Srpska, so he does not have to abide by the rules of reporting of the Ministry of the Interior. He can send interim and urgent reports but he does not have any obligations towards the Ministry of the interior because he is incorporated in the system of the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we bring up the 65 ter P3789 which is dated 13 of July. I take it that by that time Mr. Borovcanin was resubordinated to the VRS? Professor, do you agree that Mr. Borovcanin was resubordinated to the VRS by this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At this time he was resubordinated to the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then if you could explain why he sent out this report to Pale police staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although he was resubordinated to the Army Republika Srpska and although he was incorporated in the system and abided by the rules of the Army Republika Srpska, this did not prevent him or prohibit him from sending information to keep abreast of the events of those parts of the Ministry of the Interior in whose area Mr. Borovcanin was deployed. One thing does not exclude the other. Those two things are not mutually exclusive. He could still send reports if he so wanted. This was not his obligation. This is an internal document. In other words, Mr. Borovcanin wanted to, of his own will, inform certain bodies of the Ministry of the Interior about some developments on the ground that had to do with the ministry's units. But this did not fall within the system of obligatory reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I am to say the only difference on the part of Mr. Borovcanin would be that he should follow the order of the VRS superior, am I correct or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You probably are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Kwon. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm trying to fully grasp the answer you've just provided to Judge Kwon that the only difference as asked by Mr. Kwon was in the situation of Mr. Borovcanin between his resubordination and the other situation has to deal with the reporting, but you were also talking about the authorities. Is that another difference?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Borovcanin is resubordinated to a higher command of VRS unit, he no longer holds the police authorities. I can support that by an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that would be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Actually, I would appreciate hearing his example on that point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Borovcanin is an authorised official. He cannot involve himself in collecting information on crimes in the field or about the services of public law and order. That would seem ridiculous compared to the seriousness of the tasks received when participating in combat as someone who had been resubordinated to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, if he came across a situation where in his normal police capacity he might carry out investigative tasks for example, in this context he would be unable to, he would be solely responsible to carry out the orders coming from the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is responsible to implement only the orders of the VRS. That is to say, his superior commander at that moment. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Lazarevic, before I give you the floor, your client wishes to make a statement. Yes. THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN: Your Honour, I would kindly ask to be allowed to meet my attorney for a very brief period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe if I may suggest we have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can suggest it but unfortunately I have an official meeting at 10.30 which cannot be moved so there is no point in taking the break now because I have to be present for this meeting. So take your time, perhaps if you wish to be accommodated outside the courtroom while we wait and -- THE ACCUSED BOROVCANIN: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please make your own arrangements, I don't know what you wish to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I see Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wondered, because the answer seemed somewhat ambiguous, if my colleague could clarify with this expert if he is suggesting that under the example given by Judge Kwon if Mr. Borovcanin is resubordinated to the VRS whether or not he is bound by the same obligations and rules of VRS officers such as the Geneva Convention as distinguished from other rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, very fair question. If Mr. Lazarevic wishes to put it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't, we will put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think I can put it but I'm not quite sure whether this is in the scope of expert report of the VRS rules but I'll put it anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think if going through the details of responsibilities of various officers both in the police force and the military was -- even when they are subject to the military was part of his expertise, this one would fall under the same area. I mean, there's no doubt about it. So let's proceed because we are wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will put this question in order to clarify the matter. At the moment of resubordination to the competent command of the VRS is he bound by generally speaking the rules of the military without going into such detail that may not have been the subject of your expert report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the answer would be yes, although I have to add something. My expert report has to do with the scope of authority the Ministry of the Interior. I'm not a lawyer by profession and I'm not competent to study any details that have to do with criminal law or any other body of law, for that matter. I can only share with you what I know about certain provisions on disciplinary measures in the Law on Internal Affairs. However, I do not dare delve any deeper than that since I believe I'm not sufficiently competent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe you said that in general your answer would be yes. I don't think that can be found in the transcript. To go back to what we have started, I will have a few questions left for you. At the outset of redirect, I began asking you about information and representation that you dealt with in paragraph 256 of your expert report. It is 4D499, page 66 in the B/C/S and 67 and 68 in the English version. Let us clarify something. This part of your report deals with the information and representation as one of the functions of command and control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your expert report, there is a separate part dealing with informing within the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at several documents that you saw yesterday as well. First, P62, the CSB Zvornik dispatch by Dragomir Vasic dated the 13th of July 1995. Do you have that on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in so that the witness could read more easily. When talking in general about informing within the MUP, you said that it has to be accurate based on the regulations?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you look at this dispatch, can you make out at all whether Mr. Vasic was informing his superiors accurately?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that this is an urgent type of reporting, that is to say a dispatch. I cannot offer my judgement on the facts mentioned therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document P61 next, shown to you yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please verify the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: P61. Or rather it's P886. Either of them, it's the same document, I think. Yes, that's the one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, we were talking about the previous document. Does the same apply to this second document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another dispatch as an urgent way of informing. As for its contents, I cannot offer my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since certain facts are mentioned in the document, you cannot know which forces of the MUP the document refers to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I am not familiar with any facts on the ground and I cannot offer my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were asked a few question concerning the procedure of engagement of police units and certain deviations that may have existed in practice. Could we please see 4D327 next in relation to that. To cut it short, this is a document, as you can see, was sent by the Drina Corps command, document number 03/2-209 dated the 8th of July 1995. It is a regular combat report sent by the Drina Corps command to the Main Staff of the armed forces of the RS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that from the header.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at the next page of the document. [In English] Can we zoom to paragraph 9 of this document. [Interpretation] Paragraph 9 bears the title "Requests sent by the Drina Corps command to the Main Staff." Based on this document, what was the request of the Drina Corps command that was sent to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were requesting that in a certain area, via the MUP -- and they probably had in mind the top of the ministry -- to secure an engagement of MUP forces in Zvornik that would serve as a reserve force ready to intervene along the endangered axis. They are asking that the Main Staff get in touch with the Ministry of the Interior. Under the law it was supposed to be sent to the president first and then to the ministry. They were requesting for certain MUP forces to be placed under the command of the 1st BPBR, I think it is a brigade, and that such forces should be ready to intervene along the axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Which MUP unit does this refer to in particular? It mentions Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in slash brackets it says "their 1st Company."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I will no longer need this document. The next document you also saw yesterday is P3792. I apologise, I'll skip this document. Let's move directly to 4D337. We saw this order several times. You also refer to it in paragraphs 191 and 195 of your report where you mention the first PJP company. Bearing in mind the previous document, was the 1st Company encompassed in this order as well as part of this mixed unit referred to in the order?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the 1st Company of the PJP of the CJB in Zvornik. And the same company is referred to in the other document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore it is the same unit?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same unit, yes. The same part of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go to P62 which is another document we saw already. Have a look at what units Mr. Vasic is reporting in this document -- is reporting on in this document. Can we see the 1st Company there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can. Says that on the 13th of July at about 400 hours the first PJP company of the Zvornik CJB had contact with a large enemy group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, my question is this: Mr. Vanderpuye from the Prosecutor's Office offered a suggestion yesterday. Can this lead you to presume that Mr. Vasic was the commander of the 1st Company? Could such a possibility exist based on this document alone?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could say so but we all know that the 1st Company was not under Dragomir Vasic's command, although he is referring to it in this document. We know that it was a part of another unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to P3792. You were asked yesterday to explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lazarevic, can you stay with this document a little longer. This first PJP company is the part of the unit, MUP unit under the command of Mr. Borovcanin at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- while being resubordinated to the VRS. Where did Mr. Vasic get this kind of information? From whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How should I know how he received information? But I suppose that as the chief of public security services centre in Zvornik, and also the commander of the PJP, he needed to be informed about the deployment of the units that would be under his command under certain different circumstances. It is a natural concern of any chief of police to know where the first companies or any other unit that falls under the jurisdiction of the PJP Zvornik. I find this very logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me put a bit simpler question, in a layman's term. If this part of the MUP unit is resubordinated to the VRS and so to speak had become a part of military, why did Mr. Vasic have to report these things to his superior in police at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what chief in the Ministry of the Interior would not report something about the losses in one of the parts of the units of the police even if this unit is resubordinated to the VRS. So if somebody got killed in that unit, it would only be natural for the superior to show concern. It's a very human concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So one can say Mr. Borovcanin is due to report to his superior what had happened in common sense -- for common sensical reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not duty-bound, but it was common sense, as you put it, and it was normal for Mr. Vasic to report that a member was killed. I don't know where he received his information from but in a situation like this, it is only normal for people to exchange information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll continue with this when we reconvene. The break will be of 30 minutes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe that I will have just like five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, I'll have to go back to a document in order to avoid a source of confusion. This is 4D327. We just had it in e-court just before the break, so I'd like to have it back if I could, please. Could we please see page 2 of this document, bullet point 9 that we discussed before the break. When we analysed this bullet point 9, we skipped a part and it says here that due to the possibility of enemy attacks in the northwestern part of the front, particularly from the Kalesija, Kladanj, and Olovo directions, this is the axis that we may have omitted and this is the direction from which the danger may come and then in the last part it says that they would be the reserve forces for the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade on standby to intervene along the endangered axis. We would like to state this just before -- because of the axis. Yesterday when Mrs. Fauveau showed you a document about the engagement of the 1st Company on the Kalesija-Kladanj-Olovo axis, this would be the same axis that is mentioned in this document, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, and then the next document that I would like us to look at is 4D323. We've already spoken about the contents of the dispatch is, what they should contain and what they should read. However, this document is interesting for different reasons. I would like to look at the second paragraph of this dispatch where it says: "On the 6th of July 1995, at 1000 hours enemy units carried out an infantry attack from the direction of Srebrenica into the Zeleni Jadar sector, Skelani municipality. Two VRS soldiers were wounded in the attack." The last bit is particularly important. It transpires from this document that Mr. Vasic informs about the wounded VRS soldiers, wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course we know that Mr. Vasic was not the VRS commander. However, he builds into his report information about the VRS soldiers who had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to deal with the last topic that I wanted to tackle in my re-examination. Yesterday you were asked about the possible participation of units from Serbia in combat. This is on pages 26862, 26863, and you were also asked about Mr. Tomislav Kovac. My learned friend from the Prosecution asked you about Mr. Kovac, who he was and what function he held. This is on page 26852. You were also asked some follow-up questions about the command relationship with regard to the units who were deployed in the Trnovo frontline, I'm talking about the Skorpija, the Kajmans and others that were mentioned. I am now going to read to you, actually, to show to you parts of the testimony by Mr. Tomislav Kovac in the Skorpija case, the case against Skorpija unit members that was heard before the Special Court in Belgrade. The record was made on the 3rd of July 2006, it was disclosed in June 2007 and served as the basis for stipulation between the Defence and the Prosecution with this regard. I would first like to read to you a very short excerpt from the testimony of Kovac which is on page 32/86 dated 3rd July 2006. I apologise, first of all, I'm going to quote from page 34. The judge says -- Mr. [Indiscernible], presiding judge, he says the following: Here Commander Medic whom we heard, here he says that the commander of that unit himself, he is the commander of that unit. "I don't have any superiors there but General Milosevic as the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps." It transpires from this that Mr. Medic says that his only commander was General Milosevic from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says in the record from the trial, then it -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more quote with this regard, this is on page 32/86. Witness Tomislav Kovac says the following: "I've already explained that on many occasions before some other courts simply the lack of precision in leading this unit as the MUP of Serbia by Sinisa Satinovic [phoen], the others did that on purpose, they planted the MUP of Serbia because of allegedly a moral situation, the fighters down there then were under the impression is that we were assisted by the MUP Serbia which was not correct. They did not assist us, Milosevic actually blocked us and led us to a pit fall and to defeat and that is the truth. Obviously Milosevic referred to herein as Slobodan Milosevic rather than General Milosevic. We want to avoid any confusion." Now that I've just quoted back to you some parts of Mr. Kovac's testimony in the Skorpija case, I do know that you do not know the facts but would this be a possible explanation as to what units these were, whose units these were and under whose command they acted in June 1995 at Trnovo frontline.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind Mr. Kovac's function at the time as the deputy Minister of the Interior, I would not doubt his claims. I'm sure that he was aware of the situation and he obviously adhered to his statement given before the Court, and that would be my answer to your question sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you know as much to know that every statement in court is given under oath in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any personal experience of that. I've never had anything to do with Serbian courts. My first experience with any court is with the Tribunal here, but I know that you have to take an oath before starting a testimony. I did the same here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bajagic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Professor Bajagic, I'm asking this question because you are an expert in police. If a police officer while in service committed a crime, is he to be tried in civilian court or a special court like military court?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the Ministry of the Interior who commits a crime under normal circumstances would be tried in civilian court. I don't know of any special court that would deal only with members of the Ministry of the Interior. It would be a civilian court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you mean by normal circumstances, under normal circumstances? For example, in special circumstances such as the case of resubordination, is that police officer tried to be -- is to be tried by the military court or by the civilian court?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about resubordination, we said that they no longer have a police authorities, they are regarded as members of the army and I believe that it would be military courts who would be in charge of such MUP members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you think you can find the reference for your statement in the rules or the laws?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not analyse any documents of the sort. I did not deal with the structures of court or criminal law in my report, but I'm sure that there are documents but I wouldn't know anything about them, I wouldn't be able to quote any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can just assist. We have another expert witness who deals precisely with these topics. This is his only topic of his expert report. This is not the topic for this expert so you will have the opportunity to hear all these relevant laws and all the relevant documents which that deal with the topic of the criminal responsibility in all these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think in relation to two issues that were raised by Justice Kwon we have a couple of questions that I think that are integral and responsive to the issues that were raised on the redirect examination. I would ask permission to put to the witness just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt, but I think having heard Mr. Lazarevic, even ad hoc expert is going to come over to testify on these things. What are your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have two questions in particular. One has to do with the responsibilities of Mr. Borovcanin in particular with respect to his presence or observation of crimes that are occurring during his resubordination into the VRS. The second has do with his obligations under the rules of conduct of the VRS or under the rules of conduct of the Ministry of Interior with respect to the Geneva Conventions, and that was particular question which was put by the Court for which an answer was not obtained in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are precisely two topics that are covered by other expert witness, precisely these two topics which are covered by another expert. Furthermore, I believe that the witness already said that he is not familiar with the criminal proceedings with all these kind of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are not exactly criminal proceedings, the questions that Mr. Vanderpuye is proposing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also the VRS regulation. He basically said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let me confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So our Solomnonic solution to the dispute, Professor, I'm taking matters in our hand. Take the first question that Mr. Vanderpuye would like to put to you, namely --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: You are kindly requested to turn off the microphones that are not being used. You are kindly requested to turn off the microphones that are not being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He is not receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you receiving interpretation now? All right, so I will start again. We are taking matters in our hand for the time being and would like to know whether you are in a position in any case to answer either or both of the two questions that Mr. Vanderpuye would like to put to you. The first one presumably has do, according to Mr. Vanderpuye, with the responsibilities of Mr. Borovcanin in particular, in particular with respect to his presence or observations of crimes that are occurring during his resubordination into the VRS. So this is a very broad question. Taking the situation when Mr. Borovcanin and his -- the component of his team have been resubordinated into the VRS, what are or what would be Mr. Borovcanin's responsibilities in respect to his presence or observation of crimes that occur during that time? Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer competently to your two questions. Yourself, Your Honour, have noticed that your questions are rather broad and I am really not competent to deal with anything that has to do anything with the system of courts and criminal responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not precisely a question or relating to courts and criminal responsibility although limitedly so. From your knowledge as an expert on police, and you have spoken also of the situation when police units are resubordinated to the VRS, are you aware of what the responsibilities of Mr. Borovcanin in those circumstances would be if he comes to know of the commission of crimes? Do you know what his responsibilities would be?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I analysed the police and everything else until the moment of resubordination. At the moment when Mr. Borovcanin was resubordinated, I did not go on analysing his responsibility because it falls under the domain of some rules and regulations that exist in the army. I know that the army had its own courts, but I really never dealt with the details thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The second question that Mr. Vanderpuye wished to put to you relates to what would be the obligations of Mr. Borovcanin under the rules of conduct of the VRS or under the rules of conduct of the Ministry of the Interior with regard to the Geneva Convention. This was put to you before by Judge Kwon, if I remember well, and it's alleged that you did not give an answer to this. Is there a reason why you didn't give an answer? Are you in a position to give an answer now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I actually have not noticed that I did not answer your question. I'm sorry that my answer was not more complete, but I suppose that if Mr. Borovcanin was resubordinated to the Army Republika Srpska, that within the system of the army, there were rules that regulated such instances should they be noticed. If that was your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I think we can conclude here. Judge Kwon? Judge Stole? And the other questions you may wish to put, you will put them to the other expert that will turn up later on. Professor Bajagic, I wish to thank you very much on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having come over and being patient with us these days that you've been testifying. I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to ask to postpone the discussion on documents. We were unable to prepare all the documents. We will be ready to discuss this tomorrow because it is a large number of documents with this witness, so this is one of the things that I wanted to raise but I was waiting for Mr. Bajagic to finish his evidence here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any serious objection, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I addressed --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Miletic team wishes to tender some documents, the four of them, a list has been circulated. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections from your part, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So these are being admitted. Okay. The understanding is that since for 5D1318, 5D1320 and 5D1321 we only have a draft translation, in other words they have not yet been officially translated, for the time being they will be marked for identification and they will graduate to full exhibit status as soon as that is ready. No other documents, I take it? No, no, I'm checking with the Defence teams. No other documents. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do have a few but I'll be happy to deal with it when Mr. Lazarevic is prepared to proceed, if that's all right with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay with you? All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is one small issue before we start the next witness. I already addressed this issue to my colleagues from the Prosecution, they say they don't mind. With our next witness I intend to use three documents which are not on our 65 ter list, and I would like to ask for permission for these three documents to be added to our list. These are three photographs of certain area. And these are 4D547, 4D593 and 4D594. They were disclosed to the Prosecution, I think, three or four days ago. Two days ago, I apologise, I don't want to mislead anyone, and we already had a chance to discuss these earlier this morning and they said they have no problem but I would like them to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- state their position for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Silence from everyone means a confirmation of that, that there is no opposition, objection. Let's proceed. Next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, can we have just a 5-minute break, because I intend to examine this witness also in chief, just to collect my documents and my question for this witness. We just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- had a much longer session with Mr. Bajagic than we expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a 5 -- 5 minutes is enough? We'll have a 5-minute break. Thank you. --- Break taken at 11.32 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ready to go. The witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we are ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, to you, Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are welcome to this Tribunal. You are about to start giving evidence as a Defence witness for accused Borovcanin in this case. Before you start your testimony you are required under our rules to make a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth. Madam Usher is going to give you the text of the solemn declaration, please read it out aloud and that will be your commitment with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic will go first. He will then be followed by others on cross-examination. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zaric. I apologise for making you wait yesterday and today. It was because we were unable to complete our previous witness before that time. However, we may go ahead now. Although, we've met already, I want to introduce myself for the record. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic together with Mr. Gosnell and Mrs. Cmeric I appear on behalf of Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin before this Tribunal. For the record, please state your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Zarko Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The 9th of July 1966.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Mr. Lazarevic's question was, "What was your date of birth?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The village of Nezuk, Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where did you attend school?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The first four grades of primary school I completed in Baljkovica, Zvornik municipality. Between the 4th and 8th grade I went to school in sotna [phoen], Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After that did you complete any other schools?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, the high school for workers in the catering industry in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where do you reside now?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: In Zvornik in Braca Jugovic Street 3A1/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to your career. What was your first employment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: In 1985, I worked in a private catering establishment for a brief period of time of about a year. Then I worked for the catering company Stati [phoen] Zvornik and I stayed with that company until 1991. After that I worked in a bar, private bar in Zvornik until the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your activities during the war, we'll discuss those later. Can you tell us where do you work currently?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I work at the public security station in Zvornik as an expert in telecommunications.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What was your engagement during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was on the 4th of April 1992 when I became a member of the reserve police force in Zvornik. When the war broke out, I was in Nezuk, which is my birth place. I was there until late May or early June 1992. In June that year, I received a weapon and equipment at the police station in Zvornik. My job there lasted until 1994 when I attended a police course in -- at Jahorina. I spent three months there attending lectures, then I returned to Zvornik for three months and had three more months of training in activities on the ground. In 1994, I was sent to attend another course, which is to be a dog trainer, in Crepoljsko near Sarajevo. I was there until late 1995. Sorry, late 1994. In early 1995, I was a policeman in the Zvornik police station. That lasted until the 13th of July, when I was wounded as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You've explained to us your career more or less during that period. In July 1995, what were your duties as a member of the police station in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I was on the beat patrolling the town of Zvornik, securing buildings and doing other regular police tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You were talking about your regular police duties that you had as a policeman. Did you also have certain duties as a member of the PJP unit of the public security station in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the 1st PJP Company in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That was the 1st PJP Zvornik Company. Can you tell us whether it was divided into any smaller parts, and if so, which part did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The company comprised three platoons, and then in turn, the platoons were comprised of detachments or squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who commanded the 1st PJP Company of Zvornik at the public security centre there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was Mr. Radomir Pantic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a deputy, and if so, who was it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: As the company commander, he had a deputy. It was Mr. Radoslav Stuparevic, aka Raci.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who commanded your squad? Let's start with your platoon commander first.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: My platoon commander in the 1st Company was Mr. Marinko Ergic [phoen] and my squad commander was Cvijan Ristic, aka Cviko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at a document. It is in e-court. I know you are not familiar with that system, and unfortunately we did not have an opportunity to acquaint you with the layout of the courtroom and the functioning of the equipment. In any case, on the screen in front of you there will appear the document that I want to discuss with you. Could we please have 4D578 brought up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't have translation of these documents but it's basically only the list of names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, have a look at the document. Can you tell us what it says in the heading?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: List of policemen of the 1st Company of the PJP of the CJB in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look under A, it says "company command." It is not necessary to read for the record all of the names, but please have a look at those yourself and then I will have a question for you. Were you able to go through the names and does this correspond to the composition of the first PJP company command, that is to say Pantic as the commander, Stuparevic as deputy, so on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see the bottom part of the document next. Very well. It says the first squad of the first platoon. Let's look at item 5 on the document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is your name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer need this document. Mr. Zaric, I have a few questions concerning your regular police duties, as well as a number of questions concerning your duties while you were a member of the PJP unit. While you were performing your regular duties as a policeman in the police station in Zvornik, what kind of uniform did you wear?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We wore a camouflage blue police uniform with insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When participating in combat as a PJP member, did you wear the same uniform or some other?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: For the most part we wore a camouflage or olive drab police uniform with police insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, you said for the most part, does it mean that it was so or not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We always wore a camouflage green uniform with police insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995 did you hold any rank?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have a few additional questions about the PJP unit. You said you were a member of the 1st PJP company. Save for that PJP company, were there any other such companies at the centre -- public security centre in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The centre had five or six companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
