utterances.text: You have already told us that your company commander was Radomir Pantic. Within that PJP structure was there anyone who was senior to Radomir Pantic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: At the level of the public security centre in Zvornik, it was Mr. Zoljic [Realtime transcript read in error "Zvornic"] who was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We need to correct something in the transcript. The last name is Zoljic. I have a few more questions about the PJP and its 1st Company. Did the 1st PJP company include only members of the police station in Zvornik or were some of its members from other public security stations?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: All companies included policemen from all stations within the centre. Vlasenica, Sekovici, Milici, Skelani and of course the Zvornik police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As for your company commander, which police station did he come from, the Zvornik one or some other? To be more precise, I wanted to say the public security station.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: He was the public security station commander in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let us move to the 11th of July 1995. Where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I was in Zvornik that day, until that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point on the 11th of July -- were you summoned to the police station?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon, it may have been around 3.00 p.m. I received a phone call. The police officer on duty at the Zvornik police station called me and said that I should report to the station since I was to be sent in the field. He also told me that I should bring my weapon and equipment. I did so and reported to the duty officer in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you told there and then where you were supposed to go, what your duties would be or anything in that sense?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Only the 1st Company was in Zvornik, and the deputy commander of the company Svijanica [phoen] told us that we would be sent to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you told at all what your tasks would be once in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Nothing was told us about our future task when we were in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question in order to complete this topic. Before the 11th of July, did you ever before go to any field mission with the 1st Company of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So in practical terms, this was your first mission? Your first field mission?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was my first field mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you received the information and you mentioned your equipment, what sort of equipment did you have in addition to the uniform that you had changed? What was the equipment that you were told to bring with you as members of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We had a combat set with a total of five rounds of ammo, that was our equipment. Or rather, five magazines of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any other equipment save for the equipment that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't get anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you acted upon that order, and you arrived where?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We arrived in front of the police station in front of the centre in Zvornik. The whole platoon gathered there. The first platoon from the police station in Zvornik was also there and that's where a vehicle awaited for us to take us to our field mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When was it approximately when you gathered there as members of a platoon of the 1st PJP Company?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was around 1700 hours that we gathered there. I can't tell you exact time, but it was sometime between 6.00 and 7.00 that we set out for Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have already told us, but can you please tell us again whether you can remember the names of any of the members of your platoon that were gathered there together with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Cvijan Ristic, Mile Vidovic, also known as Smit [phoen], Brano Milanovic, Spasen Vakovic [phoen], also known as Spasen, Nenad Andric, Nedo Koljvitovic [phoen], Nenad Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, this should suffice, I just wanted to hear some names. The persons that you just mentioned, were they all from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were all from the police station in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already told us that you had undergone training for police dogs, handlers. Did you have a police dog at that time and if you did did you take the dog with you into the field mission?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a dog in my police station but on that day I did not take the dog with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At one point you set out from Zvornik. Could you tell us what kind of vehicle did you use to go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was a bus. A bus took us from that police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it a normal bus that normal transported the 1st PJP Company on its field mission?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The driver was a policeman who normally was on our string, and bus belonged to the Drinatrans Company or some such company, but in any case it was our driver who took us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In any case when you set out from in front of the public security centre in Zvornik in the direction of Bratunac, did Radomir Pantic, the company commander, accompany you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I don't think he was with us, or at least I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now let me ask you, according to your best recollection, when did you approximately arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We arrived sometime in the evening or late in the afternoon. After 7.00 in the evening, or maybe even 8.00. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question about that. On the road from Zvornik to Bratunac did you pull over anywhere, did you make a break?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that we had a break in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason, why did you stop?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I believe that there we were joined by another part of the company, maybe from Milicev [phoen] Vlasenica. They were all policemen and they embarked on the same bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more thing, in Konjevic Polje was there a police checkpoint there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We are now in Bratunac, you have arrived by bus, can you tell me where did the bus stop in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We arrived in the vicinity of the police station in Bratunac, the public security station, that is. And this is where we got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying this is in the vicinity of the police station that you got off the bus. Were there any other people there who had arrived before or maybe they arrived subsequently? I'm talking about other members of the 1st Company of the PJP that did not belong to the police station in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's where we all gathered. Some arrived before us, some arrived after us but in any case, at one point we were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, when was the first time that you heard that the VRS forces had taken Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I heard it in Bratunac that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Only after you arrived in Bratunac, you did not know that before?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you gathered in front of the police station in Bratunac, did you, and if you did, who from, did you receive any instruction as to what your mission would be, what tasks you would have?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The company commander gathered us, he told us not to split, to stay put because there was a possibility for us to be sent towards Zuti Most maybe the same evening or the following day. He did not specify because he did not know. In any case, we were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that all that Commander Pantic told you? Did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We were told that we were supposed to receive complete instructions once we got to Zuti Most but that there was a possibility that there were groups or individuals in the forests around Bratunac, that they were all probably armed and there was a lot of panic around Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you already told us that Momir [as interpreted] Pantic told you not to split, to stay put. Where did you spend the night between the 11th and the 12th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: With a majority of the members of my company or at least my platoon, I spent the night in a hall, I don't know whether it was a school hall or some sports hall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, stop, yes Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. I just wanted to clarify the record. There is a reference to a Momir Pantic. I believe that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just noticed it, I know what my colleague is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And the witness can conclude his answer if he hasn't finished as yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Here in the record, in the question that I put to you, there is a misspelled name of Mr. Pantic. It is misspelled as Momir. Could you please correct that as to have a clear record?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Radomir Pantic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's hear you continue your answer. You said that a majority of the members of the 1st Company spent that night in a sports hall and this is where you were interrupted.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a sports facility or a school facility, but in any case, that's where I spent that night together with the other members of my platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in addition to the members of your unit, the 1st Company of the PJP, were there any other people, any other members of a military unit or a police unit?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, not in that hall. Or at least I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there, and what happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We spent the night, and sometime around 4.00 in the morning, we got up and the commander gathered all of us again. He lined up the company. We got on a bus and we went in the direction of Zuti Most. And right before Zuti Most, we took the right turning --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. So you got on a bus and you went in the direction of Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was in the morning around 4.00 in the morning when you got up and approximately sometime after that you arrived in front of Zuti Most. Could you please tell us about the weather condition that prevailed when you arrived in the region in front of Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was a foggy morning. It was foggy where we pulled over.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you say that you pulled over in front of Zuti Most, I suppose that we are talking in front of Zuti Most as we are looking from the direction of Bratunac, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the place where the bus stopped in front of Zuti Most, did any of your commanders already meet you there, did any of them join you later?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: All the commanders were there. The company commander, the deputy company commander, and the platoon commander, they were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you there and then anything about your tasks and what you were supposed to do next?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received our complete instruction. At that moment we were told that we were supposed to scour the terrain right to the Bratunac-Srebrenica road. We moved in depth on the right-hand side from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, I need some more questions about this particular point before we move on. Tell me then, your task was to scour the terrain. In the region to the right from Zuti Most, my first question about that would be the following: That morning when you arrived, did you notice any ambulance vehicle or any some such thing in the area where the bus pulled over?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was an ambulance on the asphalt road where our bus stopped and from where we were supposed to into our mission on the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Did any of the commanders tell you anything about the checkpoint of the United Nations or anything with that regard, could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The morning was foggy and we could not see that checkpoint in front of us. But then the company commander told us that there was an UNPROFOR checkpoint and that we should pay special attention to it, that we should be mindful of it, that we should avoid any possible conflicts with them or any sort of communication with them, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thus he informed you that under no circumstances you should engage with UN members?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that day, we are talking about the 12th of July 1995, did there come a time when you did engage with UNPROFOR or members of the Dutch battalion, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No. We did not have any contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You have told us that the unit's task was to scour the terrain from the right from Zuti Most. Could you explain your formation when you set out?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: When we got off the buses and when we received the order, we were walking in a single file in the depth of the terrain of some 300 or even more metres. I remember that there was a house there and we reached that house. On the left-hand side there was a ditch or a bank, this is where we stopped, because we used that as our shelter or shield. This is where we were supposed to stop and wait for further orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's hear a few more things and then we will ask you for some more details based on some photos that you were shown. When you started on your mission, did something happen that hindered the progress of your mission for awhile?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We stayed in front of that house for awhile in order to wait for the demining squad who were supposed to take us through the minefield from where we had to continue, or rather, start our scouring mission. However, a gentleman unknown to me, a deminer, sapa [phoen], took a group of some ten or dozen people through that minefield, and on his return -- when he was returning to take the other group, he stepped on a mine and that hindered our progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you in the first group that the deminer led through the field or not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I was not. I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what became of that deminer who was supposed to clear your passage after he stepped on the mine and got injured?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: An ambulance arrived and took him away. We didn't know precisely what happened to him. In any case we learned later that he died.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to the next document. It is 4D557.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have draft translation of this document although it's a list of names but just for everyone to have it. It just says here soldiers of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade from 8 of April 1992. If I could have the assistance of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's for distribution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Madam Usher with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. If it's for distribution let's have it distributed. Otherwise we'll put a copy on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we please zoom in on the upper half of the document. I'm particularly interested in number 11. Very well. Mr. Zaric, you have told us already that the person who was injured that day was someone you didn't know, but look at item 11, it says Dragan Andric, father's name Krstonije. It says the 2nd Infantry Battalion, his year of birth and Bratunac and Tanasici. In the sixth column it says the date when killed. It reads the 12th of July 1995. Followed by a remark saying that the soldier was killed while demining a minefield. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the date and manner in which his death occurred, does it tally with what you were able to observe on that day near Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I believe we will no longer need the document. The accident that happened involving the Bratunac Brigade soldier, how long did that hold you back from advancing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: After the initial group of ten had passed, he tried to return and then he was injured. That period lasted for about half an hour and we were no longer able to advance after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you said you set out single file. Did you change formation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: After he was killed, we returned to the old formation, single file, to try to avoid the minefield. After a dirt road, we finally spread out and we stood next to each other. This was a regular formation used when searching terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think we will be able to deal with the next document in a minute or two that we have until the break so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you and we've been exchanging views in the meantime. We have decided to cut down the next break from 25 minutes to 20. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zaric, let us look at the next document that is about to appear before you. I will ask you to mark a few things on it. However, I will need some assistance from the usher and this is document 4D547. It is an aerial image of the general area of Zuti Most and entrance to Potocari. The image originates from the cadastre office in Bosnia and Herzegovina and it was also marked by their office. This is fine. I wanted you to look at the picture so as to be able to indicate to you the objects in the general area. On the left-hand side, there is Bratunac -- sorry, I didn't mean to lead. The road -- to which side does the road lead you to Bratunac and to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: To the left-hand side -- if I may have a moment. If the thing marked is Zuti Most, then on my left-hand side -- well, somewhere around here we stopped with the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Around here. And we began moving to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We will see that in the following images, but here you should mark the place where you stopped the bus with a number 1. Can you also draw an arrow to indicate your direction of movement. In the following few images, we'll be able to see that better. For the time being, could you please initial the photograph in the lower right-hand corner. Just above that --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- place today's date, please. The 9th of the 10th.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it should suffice if you just put 08. Very well, could we please save the image and let us move to the next document. The next document I would like us to look at is 4D593. This document is an image taken by Defence recently. It was taken from elevation point 438. To remind the Bench, this elevation was mentioned by Mr. Mico Gavric who was one of Mr. Nikolic's Defence witnesses. Mr. Zaric, you can see the photograph. The day before yesterday during your proofing you had occasion to see it. First of all, mark on this photograph the direction of your unit during the search operation.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I believe we got off the bus here and we followed this route, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please make the line longer so as to have a clear indication of the movement of the unit.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: In this part. I think around here there was the minefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As best you can remember, could you please indicate where the minefield was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Around this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you place a 1 next to the location of the minefield?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next thing I want to ask you about the photograph is this. Could you approximately mark the place where the UNPROFOR checkpoint was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I think the checkpoint was around here and we came from this direction which is out of the photograph. I think it was around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please place a 2 just above that.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please save the image, but first I need the witness to initial the photograph in the lower right-hand corner and please put a date there as well.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the record witness marked number 1 the place where the minefield was, he placed the number 2 next to the location of the DutchBat checkpoint. Could we save the document now so that I could move to the next photograph, please. The next photograph is 4D594. It is another photograph taken by Defence from elevation 438, we just mentioned. It basically follows on the previous photograph. Mr. Zaric, you have seen this photograph before during the proofing. I would kindly ask you to mark the direction of your unit as you went further in the course of your search operation.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We came from this part here and we used it to search the terrain. We searched this whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please place an arrow at the end of the dotted line.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course this photograph was taken from an elevation and it should be kept in mind when looking at the markings. When you completed your search operation, where did you come out on to the asphalt road between Bratunac and Srebrenica so that we can conclude using the photographs and continue with your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, well, we came from this direction and then back to the asphalt road, Bratunac-Srebrenica. We came out on the road around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you put number 1 here?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: At the end or at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the end of that route. And like with the previous two photos, could you place the date and your initials in the lower right-hand side corner.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could the photo please be saved, and for the record, this should be retained as number 1 marking the place where the witness and his unit came down on to the asphalt road. I apologise, before we save this photo, I just wanted to clarify one more thing while we still have the photo on the screen. When the unit was deployed, where were you deployed, you personally?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: From the moment when we were deployed in a line, I was on the far right-hand side so this is where my position was on the right wing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It would have been around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Put number 2 next to that.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I believe that it is off the photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you receiving interpretation or not? My mic is on so I don't know. Can you hear me now or not? Okay. Then probably I wasn't quick enough. Or I was too quick. All right. Let's proceed. But you see the problem, the problem is that once --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- it's been saved, you cannot put any more marks or it can become a new document, in other words. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, could this be saved as it is and can we retrieve a new photo and save it as a new document. [In English] something else that I had in mind. Since this is marked we can save it again and this should be a new document. And they will have two different numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why complicate it that way. Let's have a new document. There's no point in having a new document with all the previous markings on it. It will only complicate things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have an unmarked photo in e-court then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please mark the place where you were, personally?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It would be on the very right-hand side but I believe that it is even off this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that the document may be saved now. And I don't think we will need the document anymore. Now that we have seen and marked the terrain through which you moved, I would like to ask you certain number of questions about your mission which was scouring the terrain. Tell me, please, did you receive any orders from the company commander or some other officers in the company about your task and what you were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Our concrete task was to scour the terrain and in case we found a group of individuals who were armed, we would have been supposed to engage in combat. And as for the rest, nothing else was ordered. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, if you had come across members of the enemy army, you would have engaged. Did anything came up with regard to civilians, did you have any special orders with the regard to the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: If we were to come across civilians, we were not to pay any attention to them. We should have just proceeded and minded our own business, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During that operation, which was scouring the terrain, did you at any point in time come across members of the BiH Army or civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you perhaps find any traces pointing to the fact that members of the BH Army had been there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: There were their defence trenches connected with communication trenches. They were all up there in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did your scouring operation last?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It lasted up until between 1300 and 1400 hours. Around 1300 hours we received an order to withdraw and to return to the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have had an occasion to see these photos before and the way I understand your testimony, this is a rather hilly terrain above the Bratunac-Srebrenica road. From the point that you marked on the photo where you were, could you see the DutchBat base in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see it from where I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was there any obstruction that prevented your view?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: The configuration of the ground prevented me from having a better view. There are some houses, some villages, so I could not get a clear view of the asphalt road at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You have told us that at one point you came down from the hills and that you ended on the Bratunac-Srebrenica asphalt road. Could you tell me how far away was that from the DutchBat base?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was on our left-hand side some 200 metres away from our route of descent. 150 to 200 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This mean that is you came down on the road some 200 metres away from the base?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the base in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The base was on the right-hand said then?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As you descended on the asphalt road and arrived there, could you see from that place that in the base and around the United Nations base there was a large number of refugees who had gathered there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could see it well from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally at any point in time approach the civilians who were gathered there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No. We even had an order from our company commander not to approach them and not to mingle, not to mix with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Tell me please, you said that you had an order not to do that, but do you know if any other members of your unit approached the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know of anybody approaching the civilians. None of our policemen did as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As you descended on the road, did any of the commanders, and I'm referring to the 1st Company, accompany you, was anybody with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Commander Pantic was next to the bus that was waiting for us there. He waited for us there on the asphalt road. And the platoon commander was with us all the time. He was basically walking next to me. I'm talking about Cvijan Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you descended on the asphalt road, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: In light of the fact that I was the furthest away and I was the last to come down, I believe the whole group stayed between 15 and 20 minutes, not more than that as far as I can remember. That's how long we spent by the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me what were you doing while you were standing on the road?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Our task was together to get on the bus because we had an order, a commander's order to return to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you this, while you were on the road, could you possibly see the arrival of a certain number of lorries and buses who were approaching the DutchBat base in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, we encountered a few empty buses headed towards Srebrenica, towards the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to see that the buses transported refugees from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I did not have an occasion to see that. I saw a somewhat smaller convoy later in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. At what point in time, and you've already told us about the bus, you got on the bus and you left the area. Was that the same bus or did you use some other sort of transportation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We used the same bus to go to the public security station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you arrived in front of the police station in Bratunac. Could you please tell us how long you stayed there. How much time did you spend in front of the police station in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We stayed a bit longer time. Maybe five hours, after which we started gathering for our next mission. We had been told that we were supposed to leave for Konjevic Polje and Sandici and it was sometime around 6.00 that we set out on that mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And what did you do while you were in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We had to stay put and await our further orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you have told us that at one point this time, sometime later in the afternoon you left Bratunac. Tell me, please, did you use the same bus again?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, we used the same bus to leave Bratunac and go in the direction of Konjevic Polje or rather Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have already told us that your company was taken to Sandici. Had you ever been there before, were you familiar with the area of Sandici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I'd never been there before. It was only after my arrival there that I learned that the place was actually called Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you arrived at a place called Sandici, you got off the bus and what happened next? Was your unit deployed and how was it deployed if it was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: As we arrived in Sandici, we received an order to deploy in a line along the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road so as to have Konjevic Polje on our right-hand side and Bratunac on our left-hand side. Actually, we made a defence line to prevent a group or the army to cut off that road and get behind our backs in the Serbian villages that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And during that night between the 12th and 13th of July, did you stay in the same place where you were originally deployed as soon as you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I remained there until sometime between 3.00 and 400 in the morning on the 13th, that is when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let me ask this: You have told us that your task was to make a defence line and secure the road and the villages that were behind you. Who told you what your task was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was Commander Pantic who told us that there was a possibility that groups or individuals or larger groups that were armed could approach and try and break through the road and enter the villages that were behind our line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody point to the direction from which that break-through of the Muslim forces might have been expected?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: As you are looking towards Bratunac, it should have been our left-hand side. It's a hilly and wooded area that was on our left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. [In English] As you are looking from Bratunac this is what the witness said, not towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take note of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you were taken there to Sandici, the unit was deployed along the road and in the course of that evening from the moment when you were deployed and further on, what did you observe in terms of traffic on that road?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We arrived at dusk and the intensity of traffic was somewhat lower. We could pass by and I noticed just one convoy that I've already mentioned consisting of some 3, 4, maybe 5 buses that were escorted by UNPROFOR and passed by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you pay any attention to the people transported on that convoy?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, those were predominantly women Muslims mostly who were on those buses. And maybe some elderly men, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the place where you were, was there any facility nearby and if there was, could you describe it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Vis-a-vis my position and looking towards the enemy side on the left-hand side there was a house, a destroyed house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During the deployment and afterwards, were you able to observe any members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any members of the army of B&H.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until the moment I was wounded, which was around 4.00 in the morning of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you or any other members of your units have any direct combat contact with the enemy?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: On our side there was no contact until the moment I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you alone in that location or were there any other members of your unit with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: There were other members. To my right it was Nenad Andric who was wounded on the same occasion. Next to him was Nenad Filipovic, also wounded. Then there was a guy whose name I don't know, he was killed. He came from the Bratunac platoon. Next to him was Ikonic and the rest. In any case these people were there with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During the night did any army B&H members surrender to you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: While I was there no one did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone surrendered to any of your colleagues from the company?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Until the moment when you were wounded, were you able to see or hear anything that may have been taking place in the hills?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Between the moment I arrived and when I was wounded, one could hear shooting all the time varying in intensity. In any case, you could hear shooting in front of us basically all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As you were on the bus from Bratunac to Sandici along the way were you able to observe if any VRS or police units were there before reaching Sandici?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: There were soldiers, I don't know from which unit. In any case, they wore camouflage uniforms. And I'd say there were many of them along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened early in the morning on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: At a certain point after a short lull, I felt an explosion, after which I felt I was hit in the leg. And then it was followed by bursts of gunfire in front of us and my colleagues returned fire. After that moment I don't remember much. It's all hazy. I only remember being placed in the car and taken back to Bratunac to receive some first aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You felt you had been hit and you were also only partly conscious. Do you know how, by what means were you transferred from the place where you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It was a Golf passenger car. Darker in colour, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I was taken to the health centre in Bratunac and administered first aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please look at 4DP1892. It is a log of the health centre in Bratunac. Page 29 in the B/C/S. Can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Look at the first line, the first entry is 1483, is this you when you look at the date of birth, name and father's name?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the first column it says it was on the 13th of July 1995 at 045 hours. 45 hours after midnight [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The last column that was filled in says special police Zvornik. Were you a member of the special police?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, we were policemen members of the first PJP police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you were brought to Bratunac, how long did you stay there and what was going on with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, because I was only partly conscious, they immobilized my leg and transported me to Zvornik. I may have remained in Bratunac for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move to the next document which is 1DP1891. Page 271 in the B/C/S and page 19 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm being told that the document is under seal. So there will be no broadcast. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise that I did not pay attention, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir -- [In English] This is not the page that I wanted. It's page 271 in order. This is the page that I need bears ERN number 01180277. [Interpretation] Very well. The date is the 13th of July 1995. Please look at the entry beginning with 4561.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I omitted to ask you one thing. When you were wounded and while you were still by the road, can you tell us what was the direction of the attack against you? Did it come from the hills?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: It came from the direction of the hill and the forests that was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us continue now. After you were admitted in Zvornik, what followed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I underwent a surgery the same day on my left thigh. I was there for about four or five days after which I was sent to the special orthopaedic ward in Belgrade at Banjica. I remained there between 15 and 20 days then I was sent to Banja Koviljaca to the specialised orthopaedic clinic there and remained under therapy there for about almost a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You stayed there almost a year. What followed? Did you go back to Zvornik? Did you take sick leave, and if so, how long?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I was on sick leave until June 1998. The commission then assigned me to another job. I was placed at the switchboard and I still do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to go through a couple of documents, and that will be the end of your examination-in-chief. The first document is P03113. Page 2, please. Could we zoom in on the upper part. You have not seen this document before, but I believe it will be clear to you after I explain it. Under 1 it says "combat operations." It says: "On the 13th of July 1995 in the morning hours, large groups of enemy military formations from Srebrenica infiltrated the area of Sandici, Bratunac municipality and in the area of Konjevic Polje, where Zvornik public security centre police officers came under armed attack. In the course of the fighting in these places, Bratunac public security station police officer Zeljko Ninkovic was killed. Milos Zoljic, Zaric Zilko and Nenad Andric were seriously wounded while Nenad Filipovic Was slightly wounded." So that you would know what the document is, I will tell you that it is the bulletin of daily events of the centre in Zvornik for the days 13th and the 14th of July 1995. The date is in the left right-hand [as interpreted] side corner and it says the 14th of July. Does the content of the paragraph correspond to what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To conclude, I'd like us to look at another document. It is in e-court P59. Could we zoom in, please on bullet point 6. And I will explain for the record. This is a dispatch which was sent to the MUP of Republika Srpska by Mr. Dragomir Vasic to the staff of the police staff in Bijeljina, to the office of the minister in Pale and the public security sector on 12th of July 1995. Mr. Zaric, let's look at bullet point 6. I'm going to read it to you and I would like to hear your comment after that. And this will bring us to the end of your today's testimony. Joint forces of the police are advancing towards Potocari. Their goal is to arrest UNPROFOR and encircle the entire civilian population and to clean the terrain from enemy groups. You participated in the events, you were there during this period of time. Tell me, please, is the allegation from the dispatch correct, did you participate in making arrests of UNPROFOR soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any orders with regard to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: We had an order from our company commander not to approach UNPROFOR at any cost, not to engage in any combat, not to open fire in their direction, anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then, and as far as the encircling of the entire population is concerned, did you have any such orders, anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: No, not at all. Nobody ordered any such thing, we never came into contact with any civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now on to the last line. Did you participate in the scouring of the terrain in order to establish the presence of enemy groups?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was our only mission, our only task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zaric, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to try and see what where we stand. Mr. Zivanovic, will you be cross-examining this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic -- Mr. Ostojic, sorry. None?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And thank you. Mr. Sarapa? I'm sorry, I couldn't see you. For the record, Mr. Haynes is present. No questions. Now, Mr. Thayer, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President. I can tell you that it won't take the hour and a half that we asked for. It will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Seven minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not seven minutes. I'm at the Court's disposal, I can switch up my order of questioning and get a couple of small areas outs of the way in the seven minutes we have left and pick up later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do. I wouldn't like to waste these seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, good afternoon. My name is Nelson Thayer, I'll be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I could ask you just to move just a little bit closer to the microphone please and then we won't miss anything you have to say. I want to ask you a couple of questions first about the basic equipment that you brought with you on this mission as a PJP officer. You've already testified about the automatic rifle and the five clips. We've been told by other PJP officers that in addition to their automatic rifle, they brought their service pistols with them into the field. Do you recall whether or not you brought your service pistol with you to the field on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I did not have a pistol, my service pistol with me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you described the uniform that you wore, the uniform had a patch on its left sleeve, did it not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's a patch that represented the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just so we are clear on the record, this is the uniform that you wore when you were a member of the PJP unit as opposed to your blue uniform that you wore in the course of your regular police duties; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you told the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo that your platoon commander, Mr. Ristic, had a radio. What kind of radio do you recall him having?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. In our view, it was a Motorola. But I'm not sure whether it was a Motorola and what type of Motorola, if it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say, "in our view it was a Motorola," is it fair to say, sir, that as you sit here today your best recollection is that your platoon commander carried with him a Motorola radio during this operation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that it was a Motorola. It was a radio set. It was a communication device. And we, or at least I, called every such set a Motorola. But this doesn't mean that every device was a Motorola. It's a specific brand, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. Now, when Mr. Ristic was interviewed by the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo, he recalled that he had a code name that he used over that radio and he thought that it might have been Omega 24. I just want to ask you whether that code name rings any bells with you as you sit here today.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC
utterances.text: I know that it was Omega but I can't remember the digits, the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was able to use 5 minutes but I am afraid if I go into my next section it will take a little bit more time than we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Thank you, sir. We'll meet again tomorrow. And in the meantime, please between now and tomorrow morning when you will resume your testimony, you are not to allow anyone to discuss with you the subject matter of your testimony. In other words, you are not to communicate with anyone on what you are testifying about. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
